key_insight: LLM-extracted symptoms from colorectal cancer discharge notes formed three reproducible symptom clusters that were linked to mortality and readmission risk.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EHR text mining could help identify symptom patterns with prognostic value in routine colorectal cancer care.
method: Extracted 46 symptoms from 2,728 discharge notes across 1,507 colorectal cancer patients in MIMIC-IV.
Built patient-level symptom co-occurrence networks from Gemini 3.5 Flash and Claude Haiku outputs using phi correlation and Louvain clustering.
Tested cluster burden scores against in-hospital mortality, 30-day readmission, and 1-year mortality with adjusted logistic regression.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong reproducibility across methods and models, including cross-model ARI 0.727, 100-seed Louvain ARI 0.985, and bootstrap ARI 0.733, with prognostic associations for systemic and disease-specific clusters.
watch_item: These findings come from retrospective discharge notes in one ICU dataset, so external validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Large Language Model-derived Symptom Clusters and Patient Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
